projects:
1. Enhancing Flood Resilience in Tanzania: Flood Forecasting, Early Warning and Flood 
Project summary
This project aimed to strengthen flood resilience in Tanzania by improving basin-level flood forecasting, flood hazard assessment and early warning systems to support timely decision-making and early action. Key activities included developing flood hazard and risk maps, preparing flood inundation maps for different return periods, identifying critical infrastructure exposed to flooding, and enhancing early warning dissemination protocols.

2. Building the Capacity of Media Practitioners in Disaster Risk Management
Project summary
This assignment aimed to strengthen media practitioners' knowledge and practical capacity in disaster risk management (DRM). Training covered the concepts and principles of DRM and the role of media in disaster preparedness, response, recovery and risk reduction. It also focused on strengthening participants' skills in gathering, verifying, interpreting and communicating disaster-related information.

3. Comprehensive Review and Implementation Evaluation of the National Disaster Management Policy (2004)
Project summary
This assignment involved reviewing Tanzania's National Disaster Management Policy (2004) and evaluating its implementation, effectiveness and relevance in addressing evolving disaster risks. The assessment examined achievements, policy gaps and implementation challenges, considered alignment with current national priorities and international frameworks, and developed evidence-based recommendations to strengthen disaster risk reduction, preparedness, response, recovery and institutional coordination.
4. Mainstreaming Gender and Risk-Informed Development into the SADC Disaster Risk Coordination Mechanism
Project summary
This project assessed the integration of gender equality and risk-informed development (RID) within the Southern African Development Community (SADC) Disaster Risk Coordination Mechanism (DRCM). Activities included reviewing the SADC Secretariat's disaster risk management coordination mechanisms and decision-making processes, conducting interviews with key experts, identifying opportunities for mainstreaming gender and RID principles, and developing a visual representation of the mechanism with recommendations for strengthening their integration into regional instruments and decision-making.

About BRD Tanzania
Building Safer and More Resilient Communities

Building Resilience to Disasters (BRD) Tanzania is a national non-governmental organisation established on 7 March 2022 and registered on 14 July 2022 under registration number ooNGO/R/3470. BRD is committed to building safer, more resilient communities by advancing disaster risk reduction (DRR), disaster risk management (DRM), climate action, and sustainable development.
BRD works at the intersection of scientific research, technology, policy, and practical action to address the growing challenges posed by disasters, climate change, and environmental risks. The organisation promotes evidence-based decision-making and innovative solutions that strengthen the capacity of institutions, communities, and other stakeholders to anticipate, prevent, prepare for, respond to, and recover from disasters.
Through applied research, consultancy, professional training, advocacy, and geospatial technologies - including Geographic Information Systems (GIS), remote sensing, and Earth observation - BRD generates knowledge and practical tools to support risk assessment, early warning, climate resilience, environmental management, and informed development planning.
BRD collaborates with government institutions, local authorities, research and academic institutions, civil society organisations, development partners, and communities to strengthen disaster resilience and promote inclusive, sustainable, and climate-resilient development.
Our work is guided by the belief that scientific information, appropriate technologies, and accessible risk knowledge are essential for reducing disaster impacts, protecting livelihoods, safeguarding ecosystems, and creating a more resilient future for all.
Our commitment is simple: turning knowledge into action to build safer, stronger, and more resilient communities.
mission: To contribute to evidence-based, innovative and practical solutions that address disaster impacts and strengthen disaster-resilient communities.
vision: A society in which scientific information, technology and practical risk knowledge are effectively used by practitioners, policymakers and communities to reduce disaster risks and build resilience.
goal: To reduce disaster risks and build safe and resilient communities for sustainable and climate-resilient development.
values:
Our Core Values
The Principles That Guide Our Work
At Building Resilience to Disasters (BRD) Tanzania, our core values define who we are, how we work, and the standards we uphold in serving communities and collaborating with our partners. They guide our decisions, professional conduct, research, institutional relationships, and commitment to building safer, more inclusive, and resilient communities.
Our values reflect our commitment to integrity, excellence, inclusion, evidence-based action, and sustainable development.
1. Integrity and Accountability
We uphold honesty, transparency, ethical conduct, and responsible stewardship of resources entrusted to us. We take responsibility for our decisions, actions, and results, maintain high standards of professional ethics, and remain accountable to the communities we serve, our partners, donors, and other stakeholders.
2. Professionalism and Excellence
We strive for the highest standards of competence, quality, and performance in all our activities. Through continuous professional development, sound technical practice, and effective knowledge management, we deliver reliable, practical, and high-quality solutions in disaster risk management, climate resilience, environmental sustainability, and geospatial applications.
3. Inclusion, Equity and Respect
We recognise the dignity, rights, knowledge, and contributions of every individual. We promote equitable participation and opportunities for women, men, children, young people, older persons, persons with disabilities, and marginalised groups. We seek to ensure that our programmes and services are accessible, gender-responsive, culturally appropriate, and sensitive to the needs of diverse communities.
4. Community-Centred Action
We place people and their well-being at the centre of our work. We listen to community priorities, recognise local knowledge, and encourage meaningful participation in identifying risks and developing solutions. We aim to strengthen local capacities, protect livelihoods, and empower communities to anticipate, prepare for, respond to, and recover from disasters and climate-related challenges.
5. Evidence, Innovation and Learning
We promote evidence-based decision-making, scientific research, and the responsible application of innovative technologies. By leveraging GIS, remote sensing, Earth observation, digital tools, and other appropriate technologies, we generate actionable knowledge to improve risk assessment, early warning, climate adaptation, and development planning. We learn from experience and continuously improve our approaches based on evidence and emerging needs.
6. Collaboration and Partnership
We believe that sustainable resilience requires collective action. We foster constructive partnerships with government institutions, local authorities, academic and research institutions, civil society organisations, development partners, the private sector, and communities. Through knowledge sharing, mutual respect, and coordinated efforts, we seek to maximise collective impact and advance shared development goals.
7. Sustainability and Resilience
We promote solutions that address present challenges while safeguarding the well-being of future generations. We integrate disaster risk reduction, climate change adaptation and mitigation, environmental protection, and sustainable development into our work. We encourage approaches that strengthen institutional and community resilience, protect ecosystems, and deliver lasting social, economic, and environmental benefits.
Putting Our Values into Practice
At BRD Tanzania, our values are more than statements of principle; they guide our organisational culture, partnerships, project implementation, and engagement with communities. We are committed to translating these principles into responsible action, measurable results, and lasting contributions to a safer and more resilient society.
Our values. Our commitment. Our collective responsibility for a resilient future.

research:
Research, Evidence and Learning. 
 BRD Research Center undertakes and supports research on disaster risk management, disaster risk reduction, climate change and community resilience. Our research interests include hazard prevention and mitigation, preparedness, response and recovery, disaster risk assessment, physical and social vulnerability, disaster governance, gender and disaster risk reduction, early warning systems, and climate change adaptation and mitigation.
 We aim to generate evidence that can inform policy, planning, practice and future research.
consultancy: Through the BRD Consultancy and Advocacy Center, BRD provides technical and advisory services to government institutions, development partners, NGOs, private-sector organisations and other stakeholders. Our services support risk-informed planning, institutional capacity, climate resilience and evidence-based decision-making.

Our Approach
BRD delivers context-specific, evidence-based, and practical solutions tailored to client needs. We emphasise technical quality, stakeholder participation, inclusive planning, appropriate technology, and knowledge transfer to strengthen long-term institutional and community resilience.

Our goal is to turn technical knowledge into practical solutions that reduce risks, strengthen preparedness, and support sustainable development.
training: BRD Training Center designs and delivers learning opportunities to strengthen the knowledge, skills and practical capacities of professionals, institutions and communities in disaster risk management, disaster risk reduction, climate resilience and geospatial technologies. Training can be adapted to participants' needs and may combine technical instruction, case studies, practical exercises, simulations and peer learning.
trainingAreas:
Training and Capacity Development
BRD Tanzania provides professional training and capacity development programmes designed to strengthen technical skills, institutional capacity, and community resilience. Our training covers the following thematic areas:
Disaster Risk Management: Disaster prevention and mitigation, preparedness, emergency response, recovery, and disaster risk reduction strategies.
Climate Change and Resilience: Climate change adaptation and mitigation, climate risk and vulnerability assessment, and climate-resilient development.
Geospatial Technologies: GIS, remote sensing, Earth observation, geospatial data management, risk mapping, and spatial analysis.
Environmental and Sectoral Applications: Environmental risk management and geospatial applications in natural resources, agriculture, mining, utilities, property management, and public health.
Humanitarian and Community Resilience: Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH), gender equality and women's empowerment, participatory community engagement, and inclusive disaster risk management.
Our programmes are tailored to the needs of government institutions, local authorities, professionals, development partners, civil society organisations, and communities. 

We combine practical exercises, technical instruction, and applied learning to support effective decision-making and sustainable resilience.
humanitarian: BRD Tanzania contributes to humanitarian preparedness and supports disaster-affected communities during response, relief, and recovery through collaboration with relevant stakeholders, community engagement, and volunteer mobilisation. Its efforts aim to promote timely, coordinated, and people-centred assistance, while encouraging volunteerism and local participation in meeting urgent needs, restoring livelihoods, and strengthening community resilience.
outreach: BRD supports public awareness, workshops, seminars, community engagement, training activities and knowledge-sharing events on disaster risk management, disaster risk reduction, climate change and resilience. These activities aim to improve risk awareness, encourage preparedness and make scientific and geospatial information more accessible to practitioners, communities and decision-makers.
geospatial: BRD applies Geographic Information Systems (GIS), remote sensing, Earth observation and geospatial analysis to support disaster risk assessment, vulnerability analysis, climate resilience, environmental management and evidence-based planning. Depending on assignment requirements, outputs may include spatial databases, maps, analytical reports, risk information products and decision-support tools.
howWeWork: BRD Tanzania works to connect scientific evidence, technical expertise and local knowledge. Our approach emphasises understanding risk, working collaboratively with stakeholders, strengthening capacity and using lessons from experience to improve disaster risk reduction and resilience. The approach is adapted to each assignment, community and institutional context.
approach:
At Building Resilience to Disasters (BRD) Tanzania, we apply an evidence-based, inclusive, and collaborative approach to reducing disaster risks, addressing climate change, and strengthening community resilience. We combine scientific research, geospatial technologies, local knowledge, capacity development, and stakeholder engagement to translate knowledge into practical solutions.
Our approach emphasises understanding risks, empowering communities, strengthening institutional capacity, and promoting informed decision-making throughout the disaster risk management and climate adaptation cycle.
Our approach is guided by four key principles:
Evidence-based decision-making: Using research, risk assessments, geospatial technologies, and reliable data to inform policies, planning, and interventions.
Community-centred and inclusive action: Engaging communities and promoting the meaningful participation of women, youth, persons with disabilities, and other vulnerable groups.
Collaboration and partnerships: Working with government institutions, local authorities, civil society organisations, academia, development partners, and the private sector to achieve shared goals.
Capacity development and sustainability: Strengthening knowledge, skills, institutional systems, and local capacities to support lasting resilience and sustainable development.
strategy:
Building Resilience to Disasters (BRD) Tanzania pursues an integrated, evidence-based strategy to reduce disaster risks, address climate change, and promote safe, resilient, and sustainable communities. We combine research, technical expertise, geospatial technologies, capacity development, and strategic partnerships to translate knowledge into practical solutions that inform policies, strengthen institutions, and improve community resilience.
Our strategy focuses on the following priorities:
Research and Knowledge Generation: Conducting applied research, risk assessments, and geospatial analysis to generate reliable evidence for disaster risk reduction, climate action, and sustainable development.
Technical Consultancy and Policy Support: Providing technical expertise to strengthen disaster risk management systems, climate adaptation planning, institutional frameworks, and risk-informed development.
Capacity Development and Training: Equipping professionals, institutions, and communities with the knowledge and skills needed to understand, assess, and manage disaster and climate risks.
Climate and Ecosystem Resilience: Promoting climate change adaptation and mitigation, ecosystem-based adaptation, and nature-based solutions to address environmental and climate-related challenges.
Community Engagement and Humanitarian Support: Supporting community preparedness, volunteerism, disaster response, relief, and recovery through collaboration and locally informed action.
Partnerships and Resource Mobilisation: Building strategic partnerships with government institutions, civil society organisations, academia, development partners, and the private sector to expand impact and mobilise resources.
Knowledge Sharing and Innovation: Disseminating research findings, practical tools, lessons learned, and good practices to support informed decision-making and continuous improvement.
knowledgeHub: The BRD Tanzania Knowledge Hub brings together research, technical publications, policy and practice resources, training materials and geospatial information related to disaster risk management, disaster risk reduction, climate change and community resilience. It is intended to help practitioners, policymakers, researchers, institutions and communities access useful information for learning and decision-making.
